unverifiable_exemptions: Owner who occupies the home and rents to one additional person (may not, however, publish discriminatory statements or advertisements)
coverage.summary: Applies statewide to owners of any housing accommodation and to any person who advertises the sale or rental of housing. The credit-history and tenant-portion income rules apply only where there is a government rent subsidy. Per CRD, an owner-occupant renting to one additional person is exempt, except from the advertising rule.
coverage.other_conditions: Subd. (o) (credit-history alternative evidence and tenant-portion income standard) applies only in instances of a government rent subsidy.

evidence.quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
For any person to make, print, or publish, or cause to be made, printed, or published any notice, statement, or advertisement, with respect to the sale or rental of a housing accommodation
The Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA) covers the sale, rental, or occupancy of most housing accommodations in California
(o) (1) In instances in which there is a government rent subsidy, to do either of the following:

When an owner is occupying a home and is renting to one additional person, the owner may exclude applicants based on protected characteristics. However, the owner still cannot make, print, or publish discriminatory statements, notices, or advertisements.

result.notes: Set requires_unknown_facts to false. The rule as a whole covers any housing accommodation; only subd. (o) depends on whether the applicant has a government rent subsidy, and that condition is recorded in other_conditions. Added the owner-occupant/one-additional-person exemption from the official CRD page (D016) to unverifiable_exemptions. It is not in the § 12955 text, but it is an official statement of FEHA coverage that assessor data cannot verify. owner_occupied_exemption_max_units is left null because that exemption is defined by one additional person, not a unit count.
